arxiv-2102-10402.title: Geometry near the inner horizon of a rotating, accreting black hole
arxiv-2102-10402.creator: Tyler McMaken, Andrew J. S. Hamilton
arxiv-2102-10402.description: Abstract Here we present a novel classical model to describe the near-inner horizon geometry of a rotating, accreting black hole. The model assumes spacetime is homogeneous and is sourced by radial streams of a collisionless, null fluid, and it predicts that the standard Poisson-Israel mass inflation phenomenon will be interrupted by a Kasner-like collapse toward a spacelike singularity.

As such, the investigators within the ADNI contributed to the des
arxiv-2110-05575.creator: Jiajing Niu, Boyoung Hur, John Absher, D. Andrew Brown
arxiv-2110-05575.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jiajing Niu, Boyoung Hur, John Absher, D. Andrew Brown. Graphical models, used to express conditional dependence between random variables observed at various nodes, are used extensively in many fields such as genetics, neuroscience, and social network analysis. While most current statistical methods for estimating graphical models focus on scalar data, there is interest in estimating analogous dependence structures when the data observed at each node are functional, such as signals or images.

arxiv-2202-03746.title: Two-closure of rank 3 groups in polynomial time
arxiv-2202-03746.creator: Saveliy V. Skresanov
arxiv-2202-03746.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Saveliy V. Skresanov. A finite permutation group G G on Ω \Omega is called a rank 3 3 group if it has precisely three orbits in its induced action on Ω × Ω \Omega\times\Omega . The largest permutation group on Ω \Omega having the same orbits as G G on Ω × Ω \Omega\times\Omega is called the 2 2 -closure of G G . We construct a polynomial-time algorithm which given generators of a rank 3 group computes generators of its 2-closure.

arxiv-2203-12994.title: A remark on extremal stability of configuration spaces
arxiv-2203-12994.creator: by
arxiv-2203-12994.description: Abstract We explicitly study the extremal stability of configuration spaces of complex projective spaces of any dimension, and show that the homology groups are vanish in extremal stable range. As a consequence, we give an affirmative answer of the question of Knudsen, Miller and Tosteson.

arxiv-2306-04009.title: Triggering Multi-Hop Reasoning for Question Answering in Language Models using Soft Prompts and Random Walks
arxiv-2306-04009.creator: Kanishka MisraPurdue University kmisra@purdue.edu Cicero Nogueira dos SantosGoogle Research cicerons@google.com Siamak ShakeriGoogle DeepMind siamaks@google.com
arxiv-2306-04009.description: Abstract Despite readily memorizing world knowledge about entities, pre-trained language models (LMs) struggle to compose together two or more facts to perform multi-hop reasoning in question-answering tasks. In this work, we propose techniques that improve upon this limitation by relying on random walks over structured knowledge graphs.

arxiv-2402-00402.title: Investigating Bias Representations in Llama 2 Chat via Activation Steering

arxiv-2402-00402.description: Abstract We address the challenge of societal bias in Large Language Models (LLMs), focusing on the Llama 2 7B Chat model. As LLMs are increasingly integrated into decision-making processes with substantial societal impact, it becomes imperative to ensure these models do not reinforce existing biases.

arxiv-2602-05902.title: Regularized Calibration with Successive Rounding for Post-Training Quantization
arxiv-2602-05902.creator: Seohyeon Cha, Huancheng Chen, Dongjun Kim, Haoran Zhang, Kevin Chan, Gustavo de Veciana, Haris Vikalo
arxiv-2602-05902.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Seohyeon Cha, Huancheng Chen, Dongjun Kim, Haoran Zhang, Kevin Chan, Gustavo de Veciana, Haris Vikalo. Large language models (LLMs) deliver robust performance across diverse applications, yet their deployment often faces challenges due to the memory and latency costs of storing and accessing billions of parameters. Post-training quantization (PTQ) enables efficient inference by mapping pretrained weights to low-bit formats without retraining, but its effectiveness depends critically on both the quantization objective and the rounding procedure used to obtain low-bit weight representations.

pmc-10657125.title: High neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio indicates a worse response to ursodeoxycholic acid in primary biliary cholangitis: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-10657125.creator: Huiling Zhu, Mengyao Zheng, Haiyu He, Hongtao Lei, Wenlin Tai, Jinhui Yang
pmc-10657125.description: BackgroundPrimary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by inflammation of the interlobular bile ducts. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) is the only FDA approved first-line therapy for PBC, but up to 40% of patients with PBC have an incomplete response to UDCA. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte (NLR) has been used to predict prognosis in various liver diseases.

pmc-10666284.title: Adenosine Deaminase Acting on RNA (ADAR) Enzymes: A Journey from Weird to Wondrous
pmc-10666284.creator: Liam P Keegan, Khadija Hajji, Mary A O’Connell
pmc-10666284.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). ConspectusThe adenosine deaminase acting on RNA (ADAR) enzymes that catalyze the conversion of adenosine to inosine in double-stranded (ds)RNA are evolutionarily conserved and are essential for many biological functions including nervous system function, hematopoiesis, and innate immunity. Initially it was assumed that the wide-ranging biological roles of ADARs are due to inosine in mRNA being read as guanosine by the translational machinery, allowing incomplete RNA editing in a target codon to generate two different proteins from the same primary transcript.

pmc-12572651.title: Reactive co-sputtered Li–Nb–O thin films with tunable ionic conductivity and dielectric properties for energy storage applications
pmc-12572651.creator: Samaneh Jafarpour, Hamid Naghshara, Hamaneh Zarenezhad
pmc-12572651.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) has emerged as a promising solid-state electrolyte for energy storage systems owing to its favorable ionic conductivity and distinctive physicochemical properties. However, conventional solution-based synthesis routes are limited by Li loss, compromising performance. This study reports for the first time the development of Li–Nb–O thin films using reactive magnetron co-sputtering of Nb and Li targets at various DC powers and constant RF power. This approach yields the growth of amorphous films at room temperature, as confirmed by X-ray diffraction.

uslaw-usc-t47-s572.title: 47 U.S.C. § 572 — Prohibition on buy outs
uslaw-usc-t47-s572.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t47-s572.description: United States Code, Title 47 (Telecommunications); Chapter 5 (Wire Or Radio Communication); Subchapter V–A (Cable Communications); Part V (Video Programming Services Provided By Telephone Companies). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Acquisitions by carriers No local exchange carrier or any affiliate of such carrier owned by, operated by, controlled by, or under common control with such carrier may purchase or otherwise acquire.
